issues.description: Download button shown even when compiledContent is missing/empty
issues.detail: The GetAppIcon renders unconditionally in the success branch, but handleDownloadClick silently no-ops when props.compiledContent is undefined. Users will click and nothing happens. Either hide/disable the icon when !props.compiledContent, or surface a clear error. Affects backward compatibility if the backend response is older.

issues.description: Reading full compiled script into memory and inlining into RPC response wastes bandwidth
issues.detail: compile_notebook now reads the entire .kale.py file and returns it in the JSON RPC payload on every compile, even when the user never clicks Download. For large pipelines this bloats the JSON, slows the round-trip, and duplicates data already on disk at script_path. A lazy download RPC would be cleaner.

issues.description: open() without encoding and no error handling for missing script
issues.detail: open(script_path) relies on the platform default encoding; .kale.py is generated text and should be opened with encoding="utf-8". If compile_pipeline succeeded but script_path was cleaned up or unreadable, this raises and breaks compile_notebook entirely, regressing prior behavior where the function would still return pipeline_package_path.

issues.description: Download icon lacks button semantics and keyboard accessibility
issues.detail: GetAppIcon is an SVG with onClick but no role="button", tabIndex, or keyboard handler, so it is not focusable or activatable via keyboard. The adjacent action uses an <a>; this one should similarly be a button or wrapped in IconButton to be accessible and consistent with the rest of the UI.

issues.description: Fallback filename 'pipeline.kale.py' may not match server's actual filename
issues.detail: When compiledPath has no '/' segment, the code falls back to a hardcoded 'pipeline.kale.py'. This silently misnames the download. Since compiledPath should always be present in the success branch, prefer asserting or using the full compiledPath rather than inventing a name.

issues.description: Returned script_content is the .py source, not the compiled pipeline package
issues.detail: The PR description says "download the compiled .kale.py file", but kfputils.compile_pipeline produces package_path (typically a yaml/tar). script_path is the intermediate Python source. This is probably intentional, but the naming ("compiled") is misleading and worth clarifying in UI tooltip and variable names.

review.summary: The feature works for the happy path but has notable rough edges. The backend now eagerly reads the full script into every compile response, which is wasteful and uses platform-default encoding without error handling. On the frontend, the download icon renders without accessibility semantics, fires silently when compiledContent is missing, and uses a hardcoded fallback filename. There's also a naming inconsistency: the UI says "compiled file" but the payload is the intermediate .py source rather than the actual compiled pipeline package.
